steps.name: Sample structure QC
steps.context: Raw integer Salmon gene-level counts, 12000 genes x 12 samples, 3 groups x 4 replicates, single batch, unpaired. This QC precedes any statistical test and is grounded on rule R-0033 (Inflexa knowledge service).
steps.question: Do the 12 liver samples (4 control, 4 treated_a, 4 treated_b) cluster by condition, and are there outlier samples or unexpected structure before modeling?

grounding.reason: Sample structure QC: vst(blind), PCA, sample distances, library sizes per R-0033@40bf; template tpl-qc-eda@1.0.0

steps.description: Load counts.csv (12000 genes x 12 samples) and metadata.csv (condition: control/treated_a/treated_b), build a DESeqDataSet, apply blind variance-stabilizing transformation, compute PCA on the top 500 most-variable genes, plot a sample-to-sample Euclidean distance heatmap, and report library size per sample. Color all plots by condition.
acceptance_criteria: PCA plot with samples colored by condition produced
Sample distance heatmap produced
Library size per sample reported
Any outlier or mis-clustering sample flagged explicitly

steps.name: DESeq2 LRT (any-group difference) and pairwise Wald contrasts vs control
caveats: Counts are gene-level Salmon-derived but only a summarized integer count matrix is available (no per-transcript quant files or gene-length table in the data context); the standard tximport gene-length-offset correction cannot be applied here and DE proceeds on the provided count matrix directly. State this limitation in the report.
steps.context: 3-level condition factor (control, treated_a, treated_b), 4 replicates each, unpaired, single batch, raw Salmon gene counts. Grounded per Inflexa rules for 3+ groups: LRT for any-difference, then per-level Wald contrasts against an explicit reference (control).
steps.question: Which genes differ across control, treated_a, and treated_b at all (LRT), and which genes does treated_a change vs control and treated_b change vs control (pairwise Wald contrasts)?

grounding.reason: 3 groups x 4 replicates, unpaired, no batch: DESeq2 LRT (full ~condition vs reduced ~1) for the any-difference question, then named pairwise Wald contrasts against explicit reference level control; template tpl-deseq2-multigroup@1.0.0

steps.description: Pre-filter genes to keep those with >=10 counts in >=4 samples (the smallest group size). Build the DESeqDataSet with design ~condition, explicitly set control as the reference level of the condition factor. Fit DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors (no external normalization applied to counts). Run the likelihood ratio test with full model ~condition vs reduced model ~1 to answer 'differs across all three groups'. Then extract two named pairwise Wald contrasts from the same fit: (condition, treated_a, control) and (condition, treated_b, control). For samples/genes with fewer than 7 replicates per cell, keep DESeq2's default Cook's-distance outlier flagging (sets p-value to NA) and report the count of flagged genes per contrast. Report unshrunken log2FC, lfcSE, and p-values for all three tests (LRT + 2 Wald contrasts).
acceptance_criteria: Reference level of condition explicitly set to control and stated in output
LRT full=~condition vs reduced=~1 results table produced with p-value, padj
Wald contrast treated_a vs control produced with log2FC, lfcSE, p-value, padj
Wald contrast treated_b vs control produced with log2FC, lfcSE, p-value, padj
Number of genes passing the pre-filter reported
Count of Cook's-distance-flagged (NA p-value) genes reported per contrast

steps.name: Shrink log2 fold changes and apply FDR control per contrast
steps.context: Per Inflexa rules: with 3+ groups, ashr shrinkage is used for non-coefficient contrasts; FDR is controlled per contrast (not pooled), each with its own independent filtering pass.
steps.question: What are the shrunken, noise-corrected effect sizes for each contrast, and which genes are significant at FDR 5% within each of the LRT and two Wald tests?

grounding.reason: ashr shrinkage for multi-level contrasts, BH FDR at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering applied within each contrast, per R-0040 and R-0061

steps.description: Apply ashr shrinkage to the log2 fold change of each of the two pairwise Wald contrasts (treated_a vs control, treated_b vs control) — ashr is required rather than apeglm because these are between-level contrasts, not single model coefficients. Report shrunken log2FC alongside the unshrunken value and lfcSE. For all three tests (LRT, and both Wald contrasts), apply DESeq2's independent filtering and Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment at alpha=0.05 within each contrast separately (not pooled across contrasts). Inspect and report the raw p-value histogram shape for each test as a diagnostic before trusting the adjusted p-values. Report the number of significant genes (padj < 0.05) per test/contrast.
acceptance_criteria: Shrunken log2FC (ashr) reported for both pairwise contrasts alongside unshrunken log2FC and lfcSE
BH-adjusted p-values (padj) computed within each of the 3 tests (LRT, treated_a-vs-control, treated_b-vs-control) separately
p-value histogram shape reported for each test
Count of significant genes (padj<0.05) reported per test
Final DE gene tables exported as CSV per test/contrast

steps.name: Preranked GSEA per contrast against Hallmark, Reactome, WikiPathways
steps.context: Human liver bulk RNA-seq. Reference gene sets confirmed present in the environment: MSigDB Hallmark human (h.all.v2026.1.Hs.symbols.gmt, 50 sets), Reactome pathways (ReactomePathways.gmt, filterable to Homo sapiens via ReactomePathways.txt), WikiPathways human (wikipathways_Homo_sapiens.gmt). org.Hs.eg.db (v3.23.1) available for ID mapping if needed.
steps.question: Which biological pathways/processes are coordinately enriched in each of the three comparisons (any-group-difference ranking, treated_a vs control, treated_b vs control)?

grounding.reason: fgsea preranked GSEA on DESeq2 Wald statistic (stated choice per disputed rule R-0108), Hallmark first then Reactome/WikiPathways follow-up, run separately per contrast per R-0104; template tpl-fgsea-preranked@1.0.0

steps.description: For each of the three tests (LRT-based ranking is not directly signed, so run GSEA on the two signed Wald-contrast statistics: treated_a vs control and treated_b vs control), rank all tested genes (post pre-filter) by the DESeq2 Wald test statistic (stat column) — not by unshrunken fold change or by a signed p-value, per the disputed-rule choice stated here. Run fgsea preranked GSEA against the MSigDB Hallmark gene sets (50 sets, human) as the primary collection, restricting to gene sets with 15-500 members among tested genes. Then run a follow-up pass against Reactome pathways and WikiPathways human gene sets. Map gene symbols to Entrez IDs via org.Hs.eg.db before testing where required by the collection, report the unmapped gene share. Collapse redundant significant gene sets (fgsea's collapsePathways) and report the leading-edge genes for each significant set. Keep each contrast's enrichment table and leading-edge list separate — do not pool ranked lists across contrasts.
acceptance_criteria: GSEA run separately for treated_a-vs-control and treated_b-vs-control contrasts, ranked by DESeq2 Wald statistic
Hallmark enrichment table (NES, padj, leading edge) produced per contrast
Reactome and WikiPathways follow-up enrichment tables produced per contrast
Gene set size window of 15-500 applied and stated
Redundant significant sets collapsed; leading-edge genes reported per significant set
Any unmapped gene share during ID mapping reported

steps.context: Final synthesis step drawing on all prior DE and enrichment outputs for this 3-group, 4-replicate liver dataset.
steps.question: What is the full, reproducible summary of genes differing across the three liver groups, genes changed by each treatment vs control, and the pathways implicated?

steps.description: Assemble a final report combining: (1) QC diagnostics from T1S1; (2) MA plot and dispersion plot as fit diagnostics for the DESeq2 model; (3) gene tables for the LRT (any-difference) and both pairwise Wald contrasts, each with unshrunken log2FC, ashr-shrunken log2FC, lfcSE, p-value, padj, and the count of NA (Cook's-outlier-flagged) genes; (4) number of genes tested after filtering and number significant (padj<0.05) per test; (5) enrichment tables (Hallmark, Reactome, WikiPathways) per contrast with leading-edge genes, stating the rank metric (Wald statistic), universe (tested genes), and gene-set size window (15-500); (6) an explicit caveat that enrichment results depend on the method and should be treated as hypotheses; (7) full reproducibility record: sessionInfo, package versions (DESeq2, ashr, fgsea, org.Hs.eg.db), gene-set collection versions (MSigDB 2026.1, Reactome current, WikiPathways 2026.07.10), and any random seed used.

Report includes all three DE gene tables with both shrunken and unshrunken effect sizes
Report states number of genes tested and number significant per contrast
Report includes enrichment tables and leading-edge genes per contrast per collection
Report includes full reproducibility record (sessionInfo, versions, seed)
Report explicitly states the tximport/gene-length-offset limitation noted in T1S2

plan.title: Liver 3-group DESeq2 LRT + pairwise contrasts + GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: The data is a 3-group (control, treated_a, treated_b), unpaired, 4-replicate-per-group bulk RNA-seq liver experiment with raw Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 12 samples), single batch. The research question has two parts: (1) which genes differ across all three groups at all — answered by a DESeq2 likelihood ratio test (LRT) comparing full model ~condition against reduced model ~1, the correct any-difference test since condition spans 2 coefficients; (2) which genes each treatment changes vs control — answered by two pairwise Wald contrasts (treated_a vs control, treated_b vs control) from the same fitted model, with control set as the explicit reference level. Low-count genes are minimally pre-filtered (>=10 counts in >=4 samples, the smallest group size), size factors use DESeq2 median-of-ratios (no external normalization), log2 fold changes are shrunk with ashr (required for multi-level contrasts, since apeglm handles single coefficients only), and each contrast's p-values are BH-adjusted independently at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering. Sample structure QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) runs first to catch outliers or unexpected batch structure before modeling. Because the counts come from Salmon but no per-transcript quantification files or gene-length data are described in the profile (only a gene x sample integer count matrix), the standard tximport length-offset step is not applicable here — this is flagged as a caveat since the environment also lacks a tximport package; DE proceeds directly on the provided gene-level integer counts, which is the standard approach when only the summarized count matrix is available. GSEA (fgsea, preranked on the DESeq2 Wald statistic) is run per-contrast against MSigDB Hallmark (primary) and Reactome + WikiPathways (follow-up), all confirmed present for human. A final report step integrates QC diagnostics, DE tables (LRT + both Wald contrasts), shrunken/unshrunken fold changes, enrichment tables with leading-edge genes, and full reproducibility metadata (session info, package versions, gene-set collection versions).

steps.method: DESeq2 vst(blind) PCA and sample distance heatmap
minimal pre-filter: keep gene with >=10 counts in >= smallest group size (4)
design ~ condition, reference level = control, contrasts treated_a vs control, treated_b vs control
DESeq2 LRT (full ~condition vs reduced ~1) for any-group-difference, then pairwise Wald contrasts treated_a-vs-control and treated_b-vs-control
ashr shrinkage on each pairwise contrast
Benjamini-Hochberg FDR with independent filtering, alpha=0.05, within each contrast
fgsea preranked GSEA on Wald statistic vs MSigDB Hallmark, then Reactome and WikiPathways, per contrast
Integrated DE + enrichment report with QC, MA/dispersion plots, session info
